source: Measured during task-066's AC6 close-out, 2026-08-19 (orchestrator, live queryactivityruns)
title: bronze_wgi's PERMANENT-error classification is both wrong for HTTP 400 and inert against the pipeline's own retry=2
description:
MEASURED, NOT HYPOTHESISED. Found while closing task-066's AC6 by enumerating every orchestrator run since 2026-08-13 via queryactivityruns.

WHAT HAPPENED on the 2026-08-17 04:00 scheduled run. bronze_wgi failed at 04:00:03 after 167s with task-066's own permanent-error path:
  'World Bank API returned a PERMANENT error for GOV_WGI_CC.EST (page 1) - HTTP 400; not retried, this needs a human: 400 Client Error: Bad Request for url: https://api.worldbank.org/v2/country/all/indicator/GOV_WGI_CC.EST?source=3&format=json&date=1996%3A2023&per_page=1000&page=1'
The pipeline then retried the activity and it SUCCEEDED at 04:03:22 (967s). The run finished Completed. Nobody was paged, and no human was needed.

TWO DEFECTS, both confirmed against live state:

(1) HTTP 400 IS NOT RELIABLY PERMANENT FROM THIS API. task-066 classified 'any 4xx other than 429' as permanent on the reasoning that the World Bank reports bad input in-band as HTTP 200 and so a 4xx must mean a genuinely malformed request. That reasoning was sound and is now falsified by observation: the exact same URL succeeded three minutes later, unchanged. A 400 that succeeds on retry is by definition transient. The message 'this needs a human' was wrong in the one case it has ever fired.

(2) THE CLASSIFICATION IS INERT ON THE PIPELINE PATH. The bronze_wgi activity carries policy.retry=2, retryIntervalInSeconds=30 (verified in pipeline-content.json; the observed 04:00:03 -> 04:03:22 gap matches it). So the notebook's deliberate 'do NOT retry this' decision is silently overridden by the orchestrator one layer up. The consequence cuts both ways: a spurious 400 is masked (good this time, but it hid a real API defect for two days), and a GENUINELY permanent error — a retired indicator code, the exact scenario task-066 built this path for — would still be retried twice, burning ~16 minutes per attempt, before the run went red. Either way the in-notebook classification is not doing the job it was written to do.

This is NOT a regression in task-066: its 502 handling worked. Across the seven scheduled runs 2026-08-13..2026-08-19 there were ZERO exhausted-retry 502 failures, which is what task-066 was built to fix. This is an adjacent defect its own instrumentation exposed.

Ties to DEC-017's open question (WGI is annual data re-fetched daily; a multi-day upstream outage fails the pipeline every morning). A spurious-400 class of failure strengthens the case for the declined Option B ('keep last good snapshot'), so decide DEC-017 before or alongside this.

Do not commit or push without confirming with Erik first.
acceptanceCriteria: The 2026-08-17 event is re-read from queryactivityruns and the two-attempt shape confirmed (one Failed carrying the PERMANENT message, one Succeeded ~3 min later on the same URL) before any code changes.

The 4xx classification is corrected so that a status the API can return spuriously is retried rather than declared permanent. Decide explicitly which 4xx codes stay permanent and record the reasoning; do NOT simply retry all 4xx, which would restore the unbounded-retry behaviour task-066 removed.

The interaction between the notebook's own retry budget and the activity's policy.retry=2 is made coherent and documented in one place, so a reader can tell how many total attempts a bronze_wgi failure actually gets. Either the notebook owns retries and the activity retry drops to 0, or the activity owns them and the notebook stops claiming 'not retried' — not both as today.

A genuinely permanent failure (e.g. a retired indicator code) is shown to surface as a red run without being retried into a 30+ minute delay — demonstrated by injecting a bogus indicator code, as task-066 did.
Erik's half: deploy and observe at least one scheduled run; and record the DEC-017 decision, since the snapshot question is the same failure surface.
notes:
Filed 2026-08-19 from live measurement while closing task-066's AC6. The measurement that produced it: 9 orchestrator runs since 2026-08-13 (7 scheduled + 2 manual), bronze_wgi 9 Succeeded / 1 Failed, the single failure being the 08-17 spurious 400 described above. Positive control on the probe: the same queryactivityruns call returned complete activity sets for all 9 runs, and the date window was supplied (omitting it returns HTTP 200 with an empty value array for every run).

Worth preserving: this defect was invisible from gold_quality_history and from the pipeline's own Completed status. It was only visible by enumerating per-activity run history — the same class of blind spot task-059 recorded, where the diagnosis is computed and then discarded at the persistence boundary.

---

[AC1 SATISFIED AT ORCHESTRATOR LEVEL 2026-08-20 — re-read before any code change, as the criterion requires]
Run cb9be8a4-4067-4045-a9cd-35d391e2ed55 (Scheduled, 2026-08-17T04:00:01, finished Completed) re-queried via queryactivityruns with the mandatory wide date window; positive control: 11 activities returned, so the window was accepted and an empty result would have been meaningful.
  bronze_wgi attempt 1 — Failed, start 04:00:03, 168s, errorCode 2451 / UserError, message carries task-066's own path verbatim: "World Bank API returned a PERMANENT error for GOV_WGI_CC.EST (page 1) — HTTP 400; not retried, this needs a human: 400 Client Error: Bad Request for url: https://api.worldbank.org/v2/country/all/indicator/GOV_WGI_CC.EST?source=3&format=json&date=1996%3A2023&per_page=1000&page=1"
  bronze_wgi attempt 2 — Succeeded, start 04:03:22, 968s, same URL unchanged.
  retryAttempt is null on BOTH rows (matches the documented API contract; do not filter on it).
Attempt 1 ended 04:02:51 and attempt 2 began 04:03:22 — a ~31s gap that matches policy.retryIntervalInSeconds=30 exactly, which pins the retry on the ACTIVITY policy rather than on anything inside the notebook. All 9 other activities in that run Succeeded. Two-attempt shape CONFIRMED; the 400 is transient by observation.

[AC2 + AC3 DECIDED BY ERIK 2026-08-20 — both criteria say "decide explicitly", so these are answered in advance and are NOT to be re-litigated by the implementer]

AC3 — RETRY OWNERSHIP: **the notebook owns retries; the activity's policy.retry drops 2 -> 0.**
Rationale to record: only the notebook can distinguish a transient gateway 502 from a retired indicator code, so the budget belongs where the semantic knowledge is. The activity's blind retry is precisely what made task-066's classification inert. Consequence: a genuinely permanent error now goes red on attempt 1 (~3 min) instead of after two ~16-minute retries (~35 min). Accepted trade-off: a notebook-INFRASTRUCTURE failure (session start, OOM) now gets no retry where today it would — that is a deliberate exchange of infrastructure resilience for correct, fast failure on real API errors.

AC2 — 4xx CLASSIFICATION: **only 401/403/404 stay permanent. 400 and 408 join 429/5xx/transport as transient.**
Rationale to record: the World Bank API reports bad input IN-BAND as HTTP 200, so a 400 cannot mean "malformed request" here — task-066's premise was sound but is falsified by the 08-17 replay, where the identical URL succeeded three minutes later. A 400 from this API is gateway noise. 401/403 stay permanent (auth genuinely needs a human) and 404 stays permanent (a retired or renamed indicator path is not recoverable by retry). This deliberately does NOT retry all 4xx, which would restore the unbounded-retry behaviour task-066 removed.

AC5 — HALF ALREADY CLOSED: the DEC-017 decision was recorded 2026-08-20 in decision-017's 'Your Notes & Constraints' (keep Option A, fail loudly; Option B stays declined; the 08-17 spurious 400 does not reopen it). Only the deploy-and-observe half of AC5 remains, and it is Erik's.

---

[IMPLEMENTED 2026-08-20 — working tree only, NOT committed or pushed] 7 files changed.

AC2 — `is_transient_request_error()` now reads a module-level `HTTP_TRANSIENT_STATUSES = {400, 408, 429}` alongside `500 <= status <= 599`; everything else carrying a status line fails closed as permanent, so 401/403/404 stay permanent and 409/418/422/451 are unchanged. The falsified-premise rationale is in the docstring. Recorded as DEC-019.

AC3 — `policy.retry` 2 -> 0 on the bronze_wgi activity: a ONE-LINE JSON diff, confirmed by the orchestrator by re-parsing the file and enumerating all 10 activities (bronze_wgi 0; every other activity unchanged; pipeline_error_handler already shipped 0, so 0 is a proven-deployable value in this pipeline). Recorded as DEC-018.

AC3's "one place" requirement — canonical home is `docs/epi_wgi_ingestion.md` § 'Retry ownership and the total attempt budget', carrying the 08-17 two-attempt table, the ownership decision with its accepted trade-off, the classification table, and a total-attempts table (transient = 8; permanent = 1, ~3 min to red, vs 3 / ~35 min before). The notebook comment points at it rather than restating the arithmetic. THREE further docs that stated retry=2 for bronze_wgi were corrected to point at the same section (error_recovery_playbook.md, architecture/orchestration.md, error_handling_strategy.md) — leaving them stale would have defeated the criterion outright. These were outside the declared files_affected; flagged as friction.

The failure message was misleading and is now accurate: it names both layers ('not retried by this notebook and not retried by the pipeline activity (policy.retry=0)') and points at the doc; the exhausted-budget message now says the activity adds no further attempts.

AC4 — DEMONSTRATED LOCALLY, NOT IN FABRIC. The implementer holds no Fabric credentials and could not inject a bogus indicator into a live run as task-066 did; it says so plainly. `tests/test_wgi_retry.py` grew 29 -> 40 tests over the notebook's own ast-extracted functions: a bogus indicator code via all three permanent routes (404, 401, in-band HTTP 200) asserts exactly 1 HTTP call and zero backoff sleeps; 400/408 assert transient; the 08-17 shape replays end-to-end inside one activity attempt; the exhausted-budget path still raises; and two tests read pipeline-content.json directly to pin `policy.retry == 0` and to pin the notebook's prose claim against the deployed value. Full suite 340 passed (was 329). A NEGATIVE CONTROL was run — temporarily reverting both the JSON retry to 2 and the status set to {429} failed exactly 7 of the new tests, then restored and re-verified — so the pins are load-bearing rather than vacuous. The live confirmation folds into Erik's AC5.

Cross-file checks: no src/transformations mirror of this logic (grep with a positive control returned zero retry/transient/requests matches while the same sweep found all 5 modules); bronze_ingest_epi shares no classifier; test_retry_ordinal.py fixtures reference a Copy activity and are unaffected; the notebook's 6 `# CELL` delimiters are untouched with zero `# PARAMETERS CELL` markers (task-072 already records this notebook takes no pipeline parameters); `HTTP_TRANSIENT_STATUSES` at line 156 precedes the function cell at line 233, so top-to-bottom Fabric execution resolves it.

KNOWN ACCEPTED REGRESSION: bronze_wgi now gets zero retries for notebook-INFRASTRUCTURE failures (Spark session start, driver OOM) where it previously got two. Deliberate cost of DEC-018, not an oversight — but it is the one way this change can make a run redder than before. Worth watching over the first weeks of scheduled runs.

SPEC IS NOW STALE in three places (retry=2 / '1-3 retries' for bronze_wgi). Spec edits route through /iterate per DEC-016 and were deliberately not made here; filed as an audit-eligible friction marker.

issues.description: docs/epi_wgi_ingestion.md's total-attempts table states transient backoff as '<= ~6.6 min of backoff per request'. 6.58 min is the nominal 5+10+20+40+80+120+120 schedule, but the +/-25% jitter the notebook applies pushes the real upper bound to ~8.2 min (an instrumented 502-exhaustion run measured 441.7s = 7.4 min). The figure is inherited from task-066; the '<=' framing is what makes it wrong.

The same table compares 'permanent now: ~3 min to red' (a first-indicator failure) against 'before: ~35 min' (a last-indicator failure at ~16 min per attempt) — best case against worst case in adjacent rows. Both figures are individually defensible and both come verbatim from Erik's decided framing, but apples-to-apples is ~3 vs ~10 min, or ~16 vs ~50 min. The attempt counts (1 vs 3, 8 vs 24) are unambiguous and correct; only the wall-clock annotation mixes cases.

Two decision records (decision-018, decision-019) sit outside the task's declared files_affected. Orchestrator-owned .claude/ state rather than implementer scope creep — informational only, no action needed.

verification_history.notes:
Claude's half (AC2, AC3, AC4-locally, docs coherence) holds under independent re-derivation. Every implementer claim that could be tested was re-tested rather than accepted.

PIPELINE JSON (AC3). Verify-agent re-parsed both the working tree and `git show HEAD:` and enumerated all 10 activities. Exactly one value changed: bronze_wgi policy.retry 2 -> 0. Stronger proof than a line diff: reverting ONLY that integer in memory makes the parsed working-tree document compare EQUAL to the HEAD document, so there is no reserialize, no key reordering, no stray neighbour edit. JSON valid, 10 activities, 5 parameters, names identical to HEAD. Every other retry unchanged (Copy 3, bronze_epi 2, bronze_to_silver_cleaning 2, silver_to_gold 2, data_quality_checks 1, pipeline_error_handler 0).

CLASSIFIER EXECUTED, NOT READ (AC2). is_transient_request_error was ast-extracted independently of tests/ and run over 23 statuses (400,401,402,403,404,405,408,409,410,418,422,429,451,499,500,501,502,503,504,599,600,300,200). Transient is TRUE on exactly {400,408,429} u 5xx and FALSE on everything else — zero mismatches against the decided policy. Unclassified exception types fail closed (ValueError, RequestException, TooManyRedirects, InvalidURL -> permanent). Transport exceptions with no status line retain task-066 behaviour (ConnectionError/Timeout/ConnectTimeout/ReadTimeout/ChunkedEncodingError -> transient).

AC4, RE-DERIVED INDEPENDENTLY. The notebook's own fetch_indicator was driven with a scripted HTTP shim and instrumented sleep, outside the shipped tests. Bogus indicator via HTTP 404: 1 HTTP call, 0 sleeps, RuntimeError naming both layers. Bogus indicator via the in-band HTTP 200 error body (the route a real WGI re-code takes): 1 call, 0 sleeps. HTTP 401: 1 call, 0 sleeps. HTTP 422 (unclassified): 1 call, 0 sleeps — fails closed. HTTP 502 forever: 8 calls, 7 sleeps, then the exhausted-budget raise. 08-17 replay (400 then 200): 2 calls, 1 sleep, 1 record returned, no raise. Zero-retry-fast-red is therefore established at the notebook layer, and retry=0 at the activity layer by parse — total attempts for a permanent failure = 1. The demonstration is LOCAL and is disclosed as such in the notes, the doc, and the test docstrings; NO live Fabric demonstration is claimed anywhere by either agent.

TESTS ARE LOAD-BEARING — THREE INDEPENDENT NEGATIVE CONTROLS. (1) Reverting pipeline retry 0->2 failed exactly 3 tests. (2) Reverting HTTP_TRANSIENT_STATUSES to {429} (task-066 behaviour) failed 4. 3+4 = the 7 the implementer claimed. (3) An EXTRA mutation the implementer did NOT run — over-permissive, adding 404 to the transient set — failed 4 more, so the permanent side is pinned in both directions, not only the transient side. RESTORE VERIFIED BYTE-FOR-BYTE: sha256 of both mutated files matches the pre-mutation baseline and git diff --stat is identical to before.

SUITE: uv run pytest tests/ -> 340 passed in 58.27s (project interpreter via uv; macOS python3 3.9.6 not used). tests/test_wgi_retry.py collects 40 (29 at HEAD).

NOTEBOOK INTEGRITY: ast.parse OK (52 top-level nodes). 6 `# CELL` markers in both HEAD and working tree, 0 `# PARAMETERS CELL` in both; the uppercase-marker sequence diff shows only added ordinary comment lines — no delimiter added, removed, or retyped. HTTP_TRANSIENT_STATUSES is defined at line 156 (cell spanning 97-226) and first used at line 272 (cell starting 231), so Fabric's top-to-bottom execution resolves it.

FAILURE MESSAGES ARE TRUE, NOT MERELY REWORDED. The permanent message asserts 'not retried by this notebook and not retried by the pipeline activity (policy.retry=0)' — true of the repo state, and pinned to the JSON by a test that fails the moment the integer moves. The exhausted-budget message's 'the pipeline activity adds no further attempts' is likewise true at retry=0. The in-band-200 message's pre-existing 'Not retried.' was FALSE before this change (the activity retried) and is now true.

AC3 'ONE PLACE' + REPO SWEEP. docs/epi_wgi_ingestion.md section 'Retry ownership and the total attempt budget' is the canonical home; the notebook comment and the three swept docs point at it rather than restating arithmetic. Attempt arithmetic verified against code: API_MAX_RETRIES=8 and activity attempts = retry+1 = 1, so transient total 8 and permanent total 1 — both correct. Repo-wide sweep used /usr/bin/grep -rIin (NOT the shell-function grep/rg) over docs, fabric, src, tests and root markdown, WITH a positive control in the same command (the control listed 29 files containing 'bronze_wgi', so the tree was demonstrably readable): no remaining live claim that bronze_wgi retries. The one surviving '2' sits under an explicit 'Point-in-time (2026-04-05 design doc)' callout that the same diff updated — historical, not contradictory. No src/transformations mirror exists (probe returned zero matches with a positive control listing 5 non-empty modules).

ACCEPTED REGRESSION, NOTED NOT FAILED: bronze_wgi infrastructure failures (Spark session start, driver OOM) now get zero retries where they previously got two. Deliberate cost of DEC-018, disclosed in the notebook comment, the doc's 'Accepted trade-off' paragraph, and the task notes. It is the one way this change can make a run redder than before; step 8 of the test protocol watches for it.

SPEC DELIBERATELY NOT EDITED, correctly (DEC-016). Stale in exactly three located places: line 642 (Stage 1 table, bronze_wgi Retry '2'), line 716 ('Activity-level retry (1-3 retries depending on activity)'), line 1574 (Technical Decisions #5). Re-emitted as an audit-eligible friction marker for /iterate.

RUNTIME VALIDATION is 'partial' because the live deploy and the scheduled-run attempt count are Fabric-only — that is AC5, Erik's half.

test_protocol.summary: Deploy the retry=0 pipeline and the reclassified notebook TOGETHER, then FALSIFY the change against the live orchestrator: after the next 04:00 UTC scheduled run, bronze_wgi must produce exactly ONE activity-run row. Two rows means retry=0 never reached Fabric and the classification is inert again.

steps.instruction: Pre-deploy guard. Confirm the tree still carries both halves before publishing anything.
steps.expected: 40 passed, and bronze_wgi retry prints 0. If test_pipeline_activity_adds_no_attempts_of_its_own fails, the JSON was reverted since verification — do not deploy.
steps.command: uv run pytest tests/test_wgi_retry.py -q && ~/.local/bin/python3 -c "import json;print([(a['name'],a['policy']['retry']) for a in json.load(open('fabric/orchestrator_pipeline_bronze_to_gold.DataPipeline/pipeline-content.json'))['properties']['activities'] if a['name']=='bronze_wgi'])"

steps.instruction: DEPLOYMENT-COUPLING HAZARD — publish the DataPipeline and the bronze_ingest_wgi Notebook in the SAME fabric-cicd run. The notebook's failure message asserts 'policy.retry=0' as prose a human reads at 04:00. Publishing the notebook without the pipeline reinstates exactly the lie task-075 removed, and leaves the classification inert.
steps.expected: fabric-cicd reports both items published. Git integration is disconnected; fabric-cicd is the sole publish path.

steps.instruction: FALSIFIER 1 (definition-level, runs immediately — do not wait for the schedule). Read the LIVE pipeline definition back from Fabric via getDefinition and assert bronze_wgi's policy.retry in the deployed payload, not in the repo.
steps.expected: retry == 0 on bronze_wgi, other 9 activities unchanged. Anything other than 0 means the publish silently did not take — stop here; nothing downstream is meaningful.

steps.instruction: FALSIFIER 2 (notebook text). getDefinition on bronze_ingest_wgi and confirm the deployed source literally contains 'HTTP_TRANSIENT_STATUSES = {400, 408, 429}' and the new PERMANENT message text. This guards the known hazard that the Fabric notebook editor silently drops pasted lines.
steps.expected: Both strings present. If HTTP_TRANSIENT_STATUSES is missing while is_transient_request_error still references it, the notebook NameErrors at runtime on the first API error.

steps.instruction: THE SHARP FALSIFIER. After the next 04:00 UTC scheduled run, query queryactivityruns for that run id with the MANDATORY wide date window (omitting it returns HTTP 200 with an empty value array for every run) and count bronze_wgi rows. Positive control required in the same call: the response must carry the full activity set (~10-11 rows). A short or empty result means the window was wrong, NOT that the retry is gone.
steps.expected: EXACTLY ONE bronze_wgi row. TWO rows falsifies the change outright — retry=0 did not deploy, or was reverted in the Fabric UI, and the notebook's 'not retried by the pipeline activity' message is a lie again. Do not read retryAttempt: it is always null on this API by contract.

steps.instruction: FALSIFIER 3, independent of the REST API. pipeline_error_handler writes one gold_pipeline_execution_log row PER ATTEMPT, so the log is a second, orthogonal witness to the attempt count.
steps.expected: Exactly one bronze_wgi row for that execution id. Two rows corroborates a failed deploy even if the REST query looked fine.
steps.command:
-- in a notebook against oem_lh (the SQL endpoint is read-only):
-- SELECT activity_name, COUNT(*) AS attempt_rows FROM gold_pipeline_execution_log WHERE pipeline_run_id = '<run id>' AND activity_name = 'bronze_wgi' GROUP BY activity_name

steps.instruction: OPTIONAL — the live half of AC4, done as task-066 did it. Temporarily point one WGI_INDICATORS entry at a bogus code, publish, trigger an on-demand run, then revert and re-publish.
steps.expected: Run goes RED on the first bronze_wgi attempt in roughly 3 minutes (essentially Spark session start), the error names both layers and cites the doc section, and queryactivityruns shows ONE bronze_wgi row. Locally this path measured exactly 1 HTTP call and 0 backoff sleeps via both the 404 and the in-band HTTP 200 routes.

steps.instruction: WATCH THE ACCEPTED REGRESSION over the first weeks of scheduled runs. bronze_wgi now gets zero retries for notebook-INFRASTRUCTURE failures (Spark session start, driver OOM) where it previously got two — DEC-018's deliberate cost, and the one way this change can make a run redder than before.
steps.expected: If a red bronze_wgi appears whose message is NOT one of the API classifier's (no 'PERMANENT error', no 'after 8 attempts'), that is the infrastructure regression, not an API defect. Record it; it is the evidence that would justify revisiting DEC-018.

Not testable here: the live deploy and the scheduled-run attempt count — that is AC5, and steps 3-6 are its falsifiers.
